h1: How to prove adultery in the Philippines
meta_description: Adultery is a crime and grounds for divorce in the Philippines. Learn what counts as proof and how to document it safely.
direct_answer: Adultery in the Philippines is voluntary sexual intercourse between a married woman and a man not her husband. It is a crime under the Revised Penal Code and a ground for legal separation or divorce.

sections.heading: What counts as legal proof of adultery
paragraphs: In the Philippines, adultery applies only when the married person is the woman. The law requires proof of sexual intercourse. A single act is enough if clearly shown. Photos, messages, or witness statements may be used in court. Keep only papers you are allowed to have. Do not record people secretly or copy private accounts.

Filipino family law allows a spouse to file for legal separation or divorce based on adultery. The accused may deny the act. The filing spouse must present evidence that meets the standard of the court. A lawyer can explain the local rules, but KeepMyProof does not give legal advice or rank lawyers.

sections.heading: How to gather records safely
paragraphs: Gather only papers you already own or have a right to see. Do not access a spouse's private phone, email, or bank records without permission. Do not install spyware or hidden cameras. In the Philippines, evidence obtained illegally may not be allowed in court.

If you have saved text messages, emails, or printed chats, keep them in a safe place. These can show communication that supports a claim. Always check local rules about what evidence the court accepts.
KeepMyProof helps you organize your own documents. We do not help you get papers you are not allowed to see. We are not affiliated with the VA or any court.

sections.heading: Where to find free help in the Philippines
paragraphs: The Philippines has laws on legal separation and divorce. The court process can take time. Free legal aid may be available from government offices or bar groups. Look for free consultations in your area.
If you are a veteran, the U.S. VA has accredited representatives who help with benefits. KeepMyProof is not affiliated with the VA. Visit VA.gov to find a free accredited representative.
For other matters like work problems, divorce papers, or a parent's estate, free resources exist. KeepMyProof provides plain checklists to help you gather what you are allowed to have.

sections.heading: What you cannot do with evidence
paragraphs: Never suggest recording people secretly or copying an employer's systems or a spouse's accounts. In the Philippines, evidence gathered by invasion of privacy may be thrown out. The court cares about what the law allows, not what is easiest to get.

faq.q: Can text messages be used as proof of adultery?
faq.a: Adultery requires proof of sexual intercourse. Messages alone may not be enough. They can show opportunity or intent, but the key is evidence of the act itself. A lawyer can explain what your local court accepts.

faq.q: Is adultery a crime in the Philippines?
faq.a: The Philippines allows legal separation and divorce based on adultery. The filing spouse must prove the act in court. The process can take months or years. Free legal aid may be available from government groups.

faq.q: What should I not do when gathering evidence?
faq.a: In the Philippines, evidence obtained by invasion of privacy may be rejected. Do not access a spouse's email, bank, or phone without permission. Do not record people secretly. KeepMyProof is educational only and does not give legal advice.

facts.claim: Adultery in the Philippines is defined as voluntary sexual intercourse between a married woman and a man not her husband.
Adultery is a crime under the Revised Penal Code of the Philippines and a ground for legal separation or divorce.
